title: Metric Tonne, Short Ton, Long Ton: Three Tons
h1: Metric tonne, short ton, long ton — the three-way ambiguity
description: A 100-ton crane rated in the US, UK and EU lifts three different weights. Here is the exact difference between metric, short and long tons.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

hero: One word, three definitions, up to 12% spread. When a spec sheet says 'tons' with no qualifier, assume the wrong one and hurt yourself.
body: The word 'ton' is unqualified in most conversation. In engineering it never is. Every ton has a fixed definition, and mixing them is one of the most consequential unit errors in shipping, construction and mining.

> Metric tonne (t) = 1,000 kg = 2,204.62 lb
> Short ton (US ton) = 2,000 lb = 907.185 kg = 0.9072 t
> Long ton (UK ton) = 2,240 lb = 1,016.05 kg = 1.0160 t
> Displacement ton (shipping) = 2,240 lb = 1 long ton
> Register ton (ship volume) = 100 ft³ = 2.832 m³ — not a mass at all

US: short ton unless otherwise specified. UK: metric tonne in modern use; long ton in shipping and older documents. EU: metric tonne exclusively. Australia: metric tonne since 1974. Ship deadweight tonnage: always long tons.

US 100-ton hydraulic crane: 100 × 907 = 90,700 kg = 90.7 t. UK '100-ton' crane in a 1960s spec: 100 × 1,016 = 101,600 kg = 101.6 t. European 100-tonne crane: 100 × 1,000 = 100,000 kg. A 12% capacity spread — enough to determine whether a load can be lifted or not.

A ship's gross tonnage is a volume measure (not a mass) derived from a formula in the International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships. Deadweight tonnage is the mass the ship can carry — in long tons for legacy specifications, in metric tonnes for modern ones. Container ships are typically quoted in TEU (twenty-foot equivalent units), not tons at all.
Metric tonne = 1,000 kg. US short ton = 907 kg. UK long ton = 1,016 kg. Always specify which ton — or use kilograms.

faqs.q: How much does a car weigh in tons?
faqs.a: A typical mid-size sedan is about 1.5 t = 1.65 short tons = 1.48 long tons.

faqs.q: What is a metric ton vs a tonne?
faqs.a: Identical — 'tonne' is the international spelling, 'metric ton' is the US alternative for the same 1,000 kg unit.

faqs.q: Why does the UK still use long tons anywhere?
faqs.a: Legacy shipping documents and 19th-century engineering references. Modern UK practice is metric tonnes exclusively.
